title: TestInsanity project configuration
description: Project settings for the TestInsanity plugin. Every key is optional: a key declared here governs the project and is disabled in Settings | Tools | TestInsanity, a key left out stays an individual preference.

$schema.description: Optional schema reference. The plugin binds this schema automatically, so it can be omitted.

schemes.description: Naming schemes, tried in order, first match wins. A scheme binds one test class convention to the test method conventions used inside it, so unit, integration and end to end tests each keep their own naming.

name.description: Name of the scheme, unique within the file. It identifies the scheme in the settings dialog and in error messages.

testClass.description: Test class name pattern. ${className} stands for the subject class name, and (a|b) matches either alternative. Wildcards are not allowed in a class pattern.

testMethods.description: Test method name patterns for this scheme, tried in order, first match wins. ${subjectName} stands for the subject method name.

items.description: For example (test|)${subjectName}* where * matches any suffix, + matches a suffix of at least one character, and (a|b) matches either alternative. Spaces are allowed, which is what Kotlin backtick names need.

testClassPatterns.description: Test class name patterns, tried in order, first match wins. ${className} stands for the subject class name. Superseded by schemes: declare schemes instead to bind method patterns to a single test class convention. Ignored when schemes is present.

items.description: For example ${className}Test, ${className}IT or ${className}(Test|Spec). Wildcards are not allowed in a class pattern.

testMethodPatterns.description: Test method name patterns, tried in order, first match wins. ${subjectName} stands for the subject method name. Superseded by schemes, and every pattern listed here applies to every testClassPatterns entry. Ignored when schemes is present.

items.description: For example (test|)${subjectName}* where * matches any suffix, + matches a suffix of at least one character, and (a|b) matches either alternative. Spaces are allowed, which is what Kotlin backtick names need.

capitalizeSubject.description: Whether the subject name is capitalized inside the test name. ifPrefixed capitalizes it only when the pattern puts something before it, so isDark becomes testIsDark but stays isDark on its own.

testAnnotations.description: Test frameworks whose annotations mark a method as a test. An empty array accepts any method, which invites false positives. An annotation composed of one of these counts as well, so a meta-annotated @IntegrationTest is recognized without being declared anywhere.

additionalTestAnnotations.description: Annotations that mark a method as a test on top of the frameworks selected in testAnnotations, for a house runner or a framework the plugin does not know. An annotation composed of one of these counts as well; a package wildcard is matched on the annotation itself only.

items.description: A fully qualified annotation name, or a package wildcard ending in .* which matches every annotation in that package and below.

includeInheritedMethods.description: Match methods inherited from a base class, not only methods declared in the class itself.

includeInterfacesAndAbstracts.description: Treat interfaces and abstract classes as test classes when their name matches a pattern.

includeNestedClasses.description: Match test methods declared in nested classes, such as JUnit 5 @Nested.

syncDisplayName.description: Generate a JUnit 5 @DisplayName on created test methods, and keep a generated one in sync when the method is renamed. A DisplayName written by hand is never overwritten.

refactoring.description: Propose the sibling renames when a class or method is renamed.

navigation.description: Offer Jump to Sibling, and answer the IDE own Navigate | Test with this naming scheme.

gutterIcons.description: Show the sibling class or method in the gutter.

preselectRenames.description: Start the proposed sibling renames checked in the Rename related items dialog.
